The person on the right is in a standing position, with the person on the left being thrown. This indicates a demonstration of the Tsuriotoshi technique by a named 4th Dan judoka. The illustration originates from a judo instruction book from the Meiji era. The scene then transitions to a vintage black-and-white video of a man in a white uniform throwing another man in a dark uniform to the ground. This is followed by another image of a judo throw from a vintage book. The text below this image says "写真11 大腰分 [日本百科大辞典] 明治43年" ("Photo 11: Ogoshi, [Japanese Encyclopedia], Meiji 43 year"), which indicates that the image depicts the "Ogoshi" throw and is sourced from a Japanese encyclopedia during the Meiji period.

The video segment showcases a martial arts demonstration, specifically focusing on the "Yoko-wakare" technique. Initially, a black-and-white sketch from 1910 of two people locked in a Judo-like grapple is depicted. Text below this drawing reads “写真11 大横分「日本百科大辞典」明治43年” (“Photo 11. Oyokowake "Great Japanese Encyclopedia" Meiji 43”), indicating that the image is from a historical encyclopedia. Transitioning to a modern setting with a light blue background, two individuals dressed in white judo uniforms demonstrate the technique. The person in the white uniform with a black belt, grips the uniform of the person in the white uniform with a red belt, and the instructor drops their weight while using their hands to pull the red belt individual to the side and onto the floor. The text on the bottom of the screen reads "Yoko-wakare," identifying the demonstrated maneuver.
